Engine skipped: estimated JPEG quality factor 74 is at or below 85, where Ferrara et al. state their algorithm 'is unable to discriminate between the presence and absence of CFA artifacts'. Compression has erased the demosaicing correlation this engine measures.
images.reasoning: Engine reported raw_score=0.000000 (reduction rule 'max' over the per-block tampering map) at confidence 0.0000, is_reliable=False. With the JPEG-quality gate bypassed for diagnosis the same image yields raw_score=0.5777868753830039, probability=None, 41 flagged region(s). Feature stage: {}. Posterior/mixture stage: {}. Grid-consistency layer: {}.
images.mathematical_explanation: Ferrara's pipeline extracts the green channel, forms the bilinear prediction error e(x,y) of Eq. 9, takes its locally-weighted variance over a Gaussian window of standard deviation K/2 restricted to each lattice class (Eq. 10), and reduces each block to L = log(GM_A/GM_I) (Eq. 11-12) - the log ratio of prediction-error variance at acquired versus interpolated Bayer positions. Under M1 (CFA intact) Eq. 13 requires this to be positive; under M2 (CFA destroyed) Eq. 14 fixes its mean at zero. For this image the fitted mixture reported {}. The per-block posterior Pr(M1|L) of Eq. 15-17 is then inverted to a tampering map and reduced to the scalar above. The engine's own gate matters here more than the arithmetic: the SKILL states demosaicing correlation is the dominant casualty of JPEG compression, and this image's estimated quality factor is 74.

Ferrara et al. state the method 'is less effective in the presence of either almost flat areas or sharp edges', so the surviving blocks are not a representative sample of the scene. The SKILL file specifies no calibration function for this statistic and leaves the map reduction rule itself as an engineering recommendation, so this probability expresses relative ordering only and must not be read as a literal likelihood. The raw score and the per-block map are the trustworthy quantities.
